chapter: Recent years and early piano influences
title: Hearing Clarence Profit, Hines and J.P. Johnson on radio
summary: He heard Profit at the Cave, other pianists named Norton, Earl Hines's innovation and J.P. Johnson's style.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Then of course, I heard Clarence Profit...
Ramirez - 146
Where did you hear him first?
I heard him at a place called the Cave, where the kids used to go when I was about...
Oh yes.

I was about 15 or 16 years old, 15... As I said before, we had little places where kids went that they called...they had teas. And he was playing there. This is where I was so impressed about him, you know.

There was another one called Joe Norton. And there was another Norton who used to stride and play California, a White guy. Two Nortons. They were spelled differently, I think. This is when I started playing...trying...you know, playing Jazz.
Would most of those guys be playing Stride?
Yes. Well, that was the thing of the day. Earl Hines came with a different innovation, so...
He really changed it around.

Yeah, he was more radical. Usually in those years, you know... New York is... There was so much happening in New York in my childhood that... You know, I became aware about this music coming over the wireless -- is that what you say?
In those days it was all wireless.
Yeah. Then of course, that's when the Cotton
Ramirez - 147
Club Jungle Band used to come on -- Duke Ellington's band. I lost my point...
Of course, what you heard on the radio then was not records, was it.
No, it was live. In those days they didn't have disk jockeys or anything like that to play recordings.
But guys like Clarence Profit wouldn't get on the radio, would they.

Yeah, he was coming over WHN, alternating with the Red Devil Stompers. I had heard of J.P. Johnson. He played the style of J.P. Johnson, he did Fats Waller. But I never met J.P. Johnson until much later, when I was going to high school, and when Art Tatum came into New York. But he was the first, like, impression of that style that I... I mean, he was the impression of that style until I heard J.P. himself play it...you know, that impressed me.
Where did you hear Fats?
I heard Fats much later. I heard him in, as I said before, the Alhambra -- the Alhambra Theatre.
